business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Air Freight Forwarding and Cargo Aircraft Charter

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Unitary National Jurisdiction; provincial Mercantile Registries coordinated by the Registro Mercantil Central)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European codified system with strong notarial and registry safeguards)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain–United States Income Tax Treaty (1990, as amended by 2013 Protocol)
Spain–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (2005) and DTA (1990, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (reglamento de la Ley 10/2010); Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio, por el que se crea el Registro Único de Titularidades Reales; Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo, de reforma de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (UBO and corporate transparency); supervision by SEPBLAC, Banco de España, and the Consejo General del Notariado
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (Spanis UBO register is not fully public; access restricted to competent authorities — AEAT, SEPBLAC, CNMV, DGPNSD — and to obliged entities upon demonstration of legitimate interest, consistent with CJEU proportionality jurisprudence)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the existing corporate shareholder, issued by its home registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Companies Registry or Chamber of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (origin state party to the 1961 Apostille Convention) OR Consular Legalization (non-Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Officers of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country registry or authorized corporate service provider

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial-Owner Declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real) executed before the Spanish Notary within the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial act incorporated into the public deed; no external apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority; bank or utility supplier
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or notary-certified copy; foreign-issued address proof to be legalized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing legitimacy of source of funds of the contributing member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originator bank of the shareholder or contributing party
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature; apostille recommended where the issuing bank is abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (when the incorporator acts through a proxy before the Spanish Notary)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all directors, UBOs, signatories, and material counterparties against PEP databases, OFAC SDN list, UN consolidated sanctions, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions list, and the Spanish Council of Ministers asset-freezing list; enhanced due diligence required where the corporate seat, freight origin/destination, counterparty, or payment rails (Swift/Wire) touch high-risk jurisdictions; negative news monitoring aligned with SEPBLAC guidance and FATF public statements; historical review of corporate criminal and AML records for all officers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central — official portal: www.rmc.es (negative name certification service interoperable with provincial registries and notaries)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate denomination must be written in Spanish (Latin script); foreign-language names are admissible but must be transliterated into Spanish characters and must not be misleading; the legal-form suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.' is mandatory; the name must be unique and must not be identical or phonetically/structurally confusable with an existing Spanish or EU-registered denomination.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España, Estado, Gobierno, Administración, Ministerio (state-identity tokens requiring prior ministerial authorization)
Banco, Caja, Seguros, Reaseguros, Asistencia Sanitaria, Mutualidad (regulated financial and health tokens requiring prior sector-licensing approval)
S.A., S.A.U., S.L.N.E., Sociedad Anónima, Sociedad Unipersonal (legal-form tokens inconsistent with the intended SL structure)
Tokens contrary to law, morality, or public order, or which may constitute a criminal offense (Article 407, Ley de Sociedades de Capital)
Denominations identical or misleadingly similar to any existing registered Spanish or EU company name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social) is valid for three months and is non-renewable. Upon rejection, the incorporator may (i) immediately submit a corrective denomination application via the RMC portal, or (ii) file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (Ministry of Justice) within one month of the refusal notice under Ley 39/2015 (LPACAP); the granted certificate must be embedded in the notarial deed of incorporation before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Administratively permissible only as a temporary auxiliary correspondence address; for the air-cargo charter brokerage model, substance tolerance is low — Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital requires the domicilio social to be the genuine seat of management, and AEAT residence tests, SEPBLAC substance expectations, and IATA/AESA cargo-agent accreditation require a physical managed office with personnel and operational records; a serviced office may be used during ramp-up but must be replaced by a substantive physical establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-high quantified risk: approximately 40% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation, anticipated from AEAT (VAT registration and substance audits), SEPBLAC (AML on-site examination), or AESA/IATA accreditation audits for freight-forwarding license maintenance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; fixed corporate-formation and AML compliance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff (Arancel de los Notarios, Ministry of Justice)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the notarial deed in the Provincial Commercial Registry (inscripción en el Registro Mercantil)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff (Arancel del Registro Mercantil)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) application for non-resident directors and UBOs
Sworn translation and apostilization of foreign corporate documents (Certificate of Good Standing, Incumbency, passports, Powers of Attorney)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; approximately EUR 90–120 per sworn translation document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized copies, protocoling, and legalization of shareholder and security documentation
Corporate bank account opening and AML/KYC onboarding package (Swift and Fedwire rails support)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published tariff — account opening and compliance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SEPBLAC / Registro Único de Titularidades Reales filing and initial AML compliance subscription
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Ministry of Finance (SEPBLAC regime) and compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative filing fee plus market compliance retainer

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional AEAT fiscal registration — provisional NIF (CIF) and census of entrepreneurs (censo de empresarios)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fee-exempt statutory procedure (Article 22, Ley General Tributaria)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 4, 20-24, 29-32, 33-35, 38-40, 43, 78-79, 210-242, and 249; Law 14/2013 on entrepreneurs and electronic incorporation procedures; and Royal Decree 1784/1996 approving the Mercantile Registry Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, coordinated through the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), executed before a Spanish notary and filed for registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry, together with the approved articles of association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum share capital of an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid at incorporation. Until capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and subscribed capital if the company is wound up with insufficient assets. A separate escrow account is not generally mandatory; payment may be evidenced by a bank certificate or, under applicable statutory conditions, by the founders' declaration of responsibility in the incorporation deed. Notarial, registry, publication, tax-administration, and professional fees are separate from any state filing charge.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of [Company Name], S.L., resolves that: (1) the subscribed share capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] shares of EUR [nominal value] each, is approved as fully subscribed and paid; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted; (3) [name] is appointed sole director/chairman, and [name] is appointed secretary, each accepting office and declaring no legal incompatibility; (4) the director is authorized to obtain the NIF, register the company with tax and employment authorities, open bank accounts, and complete all aviation, customs, municipal, and operational filings; and (5) the secretary shall enter this resolution in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), online name-certification service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-clearance request listing preferred names in priority order. Obtain the negative name certificate, which is generally valid for three months for execution of the deed and six months for reservation purposes. Ensure the proposed name includes the legal suffix Sociedad Limitada or S.L.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name request and correct any similarity, prohibited-term, or legal-form defect. Preserve the certificate and use the exact certified name in all subsequent documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Investor Identification and Tax Documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) and, for non-resident individuals or entities, the relevant Spanish consular post or authorized representative channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Spanish foreigner identification number (NIE) for non-resident individual founders and a Spanish tax identification number (NIF) for non-resident corporate founders. Legalize or apostille foreign corporate documents and provide certified Spanish translations where required. Confirm beneficial-owner information before the notarial appointment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to AEAT or consular queries with corrected identity, legalization, translation, or beneficial-ownership documents. Refile through an authorized tax representative if the applicant lacks a Spanish electronic identification method.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary Public (Notario Público) selected by the founders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the negative name certificate, articles of association, founder identification, NIE or NIF evidence, beneficial-owner declaration, registered-office evidence, capital-payment evidence, and powers of attorney. Execute the public deed in Spanish or through an authorized interpreter. The deed must identify the founders, contributions, shares, corporate purpose, registered office, management structure, and initial directors.
required_dossiers: Proof of capital payment or statutory payment declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct defective articles, authority evidence, capital documentation, or identity records before signing. If the deed has already been executed, request a corrective public deed or notarial rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered office, normally through the notary's electronic filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized incorporation deed electronically or in certified hard copy, together with the required registry forms and payment of the applicable registry tariff. Verify that the corporate purpose accurately distinguishes brokerage and freight-forwarding activities from regulated air-carrier operations. Obtain the registration entry and certified registry extract.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a qualification notice, cure each defect within the applicable statutory period by notarial correction, supplementary filing, or documentary clarification. Appeal the qualification to the Directorate-General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith or the competent court where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Beneficial-Owner, and Accounting Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT), Provincial Mercantile Registry, and the relevant regional or municipal tax offices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain or confirm the definitive NIF, register the activity through the applicable census declaration, select VAT and corporate-tax obligations, and assess Intrastat, customs, and cross-border reporting requirements. Legalize the company's electronic books and establish statutory accounting, invoicing, beneficial-owner, and annual filing controls.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct census classifications, VAT status, activity codes, or beneficial-owner filings through amended AEAT or registry submissions. Preserve submission receipts and obtain written clarification for disputed classifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Corporate Governance and Compliance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's governing body, Provincial Mercantile Registry, AEAT, and the Spanish Data Protection Agency where relevant.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board or sole-director resolutions, approve bank signatories, appoint compliance and data-protection contacts, maintain the minutes book and shareholder register, and implement powers-of-attorney controls. If employees are engaged, register the employer with Social Security before commencement and complete occupational-risk and workplace notifications.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Ratify omitted approvals through a properly convened shareholder or board meeting, correct corporate books, and submit late employment or workplace filings with any applicable surcharge or explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Aviation, Customs, and Physical-Operations Authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Aviation Safety Agency (Agencia Estatal de Seguridad Aérea, AESA), Spanish Tax Agency Customs Department, airport operator, and competent autonomous-community or municipal authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the company acts solely as a broker or will perform regulated freight-forwarding, customs-representation, warehouse, security, or air-carrier functions. A broker must use an appropriately licensed air carrier for flights and must not hold itself out as the operator. Apply separately for customs-representative status, regulated-agent or known-consignor status, airport access, warehouse activity, and any carrier authorization that the actual operating model requires.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to AESA, customs, airport, or municipal deficiency notices within the stated period; amend the operating model where it inadvertently constitutes air carriage; and appeal an adverse aviation decision under the applicable administrative procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Aviation Safety Agency (Agencia Estatal de Seguridad Aérea, AESA) for regulated air-transport activities; the relevant Autonomous Community industrial authority and municipality for premises, installations, and activity licensing; and the Spanish Tax Agency Customs Department for customs-related services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: For a pure air-cargo charter broker, no standalone Spanish air-carrier operating licence is normally required if the company neither operates aircraft nor sells transport as the carrier. The contracted air carrier must hold an EU Air Operator Certificate (AOC) and, where applicable, an Operating Licence under Regulation (EC) No 1008/2008. The broker may additionally require customs-representation authorization, regulated-agent or known-consignor approval under aviation-security rules, airport authorization, and a municipal opening or activity licence for physical premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), together with the competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from a project-level EIA for a desk-based brokerage office. A warehouse, cargo terminal, fuel installation, major airport infrastructure, or material modification may require environmental screening or a simplified or ordinary EIA under Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment and applicable regional rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: A brokerage office generally has no process wastewater or industrial VOC emissions. Any warehouse or facility must comply with applicable municipal discharge permits, Law 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils, producer and hazardous-waste rules, packaging obligations, and regional air-emission requirements. Hazardous waste must be segregated, documented, stored safely, and transferred to authorized waste managers; no wastewater, VOC, or waste stream may be discharged without the applicable permit or authorization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Physical premises require municipal activity or opening authorization, fire-prevention compliance under the Spanish Building Code and applicable fire-safety regulations, emergency planning, and documented evacuation arrangements. Warehouses and cargo areas may require structural-load certification, electrical and installation certificates, fire-protection inspection, occupational-risk assessment under Law 31/1995, worker training, and workplace notification to the competent Autonomous Community authority. Airport premises additionally require the airport operator's safety, access, and security approvals.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); administrative registry and VAT registration via censal forms 036/037; SII and customs filings through AEAT Web Services (API/SOAP) and the SED-4.0 customs clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity incorporating an SL must obtain a provisional Spanish Tax Identification Number (NIF) before execution of the public deed by filing Form 036 with AEAT through the notary or the 'NIF provisional' procedure. After the mercantile registry inscription, the definitive NIF is issued (entity prefix N/B), and the company must file the definitive declaración censal de alta (Modelo 036) within one month. Non-resident entities acting without a permanent establishment must obtain a Non-Resident NIF (NIF-NR) using Modelo 030 (individuals) or Modelo 036 (entities), including supporting legalized incorporation documents, apostille, and power of attorney registered with AEAT. VAT identification (NIF-IVA) is requested via the same censal filing; an air-cargo charter broker engaging in B2B international freight services must additionally assess whether a fixed establishment in Spain triggers NIF-PE registration. All requests are processed through AEAT's Registro Censal, with response typically within 2–4 weeks for non-residents and immediate provisional issuance for resident incorporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (an SL is a separate taxpayer under the Corporate Income Tax Law, Ley 27/2014; resident entities are subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades on worldwide income; no general pass-through election exists; the only transparency regimes are the AIE/UTE special régime and certain EU-free-zone provisions, which are non-default elective structures).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no check-the-box election. Available statutory elections include: the consolidated tax group régime (arts. 58–70 Ley 27/2014) for 75%+ Spanish-consolidated groups; the neutrality régime for mergers and share-for-share exchanges (arts. 76–86); the ETVE international holding régime; the 15% reduced CIT rate for newly created SLs (art. 29.1) where revenue in the first two years is below EUR 1,000,000 and no dormant-capital activity exists; the simplified VAT régimes for small traders; the OSS/IOSS one-stop-shop elections for intra-EU distance sales and e-services; the patent-box régime; and the Special Fiscal Regime for Canary Islands (ZEC). Hybrid mismatch anti-double-dip rules were implemented by Ley 11/2021 (transposing ATAD 2) and restrict deductible interest, dividends or payments allocable to hybrid vehicles; these operate as mandatory anti-abuse provisions, not elective classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) – Spanish VAT governed by Ley 37/1992 (LIVA) and Real Decreto 1624/1992, harmonized with EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general national turnover threshold for VAT registration in Spain; any person carrying out taxable transactions in Spanish taxable territory must be registered from the first euro. For non-established EU and third-country suppliers of intra-EU distance sales of goods and B2C electronic services, the registration obligation arises after exceeding the EUR 10,000 Union-wide intra-EU distance-sales threshold; below that threshold the OSS simplifies compliance. For B2B air-cargo charter brokerage, Spanish VAT is not chargeable where the recipient is a taxable person established outside Spain and the place-of-supply rules (arts. 69–70 LIVA) locate the supply outside Spain; nevertheless, a Spanish fixed establishment or economic activity by the broker would create a mandatory Spanish VAT registration regardless of billing volume.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Large taxpayers (turnover above EUR 6,000,000, VAT groups, and cash-basis taxpayers) are mandatorily subject to the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) real-time record-filing régime: invoice records for sales and purchases must be transmitted electronically to AEAT within 4 business days of issue or receipt (extended to 8 business days in August), using AEAT Web Services (SOAP/XML) with automatic validation. Real Decreto 1007/2023 (Verifactu) introduces, from 1 January 2025 for new billing software and from 1 January 2026 for all systems, the duty to use certified invoicing programs producing tamper-proof invoice records with a unique QR-linked hash chain ('Huella') enabling interoperability with AEAT. The Basque provinces (Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa, Álava) already mandate TicketBAI real-time digital stamping of B2B/B2C invoices. Customs clearance for exported air-cargo shipments is fully electronic through the DUA procedure (Mensaje de Datos de Despacho) in the SED-4.0 environment, with integrated AES/ICS messaging via CCI/API channels.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical exports of goods to third countries or territories (art. 21.1 LIVA) are exempt with the right to deduction (zero-rated) once the goods are officially declared for export in the DUA and physically leave the EU within 3 months of the date of supply or dispatch. Intra-Community supplies (art. 25 LIVA) qualify for zero-rating when the buyer communicates a valid EU VAT ID verified in VIES, the goods are dispatched to another Member State, and the supplier files the recapitulative statement (Modelo 349). For an air-cargo charter broker, zero-rating also applies to international transport of goods and ancillary services directly connected with export cargo (art. 26–28 LIVA) and to B2B intermediation services where the place of supply is outside Spain (no Spanish VAT where the recipient's establishment is outside the EU). Documentary adherence must evidence the physical movement and the commercial reality of the freight transaction; the air waybill (MAWB/HAWB), customs export declaration, and proof of arrival are indispensable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA / Mensaje de Datos de Despacho) stamped or electronically released by Spanish Customs
Master Air Waybill (MAWB) and House Air Waybill (HAWB) showing the SL as shipper, agent, or intermediary and evidencing the airport-of-departure and final destination
Bill of Lading or Cargo Manifest
Commercial Invoice and packing list aligned to weight/HS codes
Proof of arrival at destination (if available, customs gate report, arrival notice, or consignee receipt)
Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de cobro al exterior) or bank SWIFT/Fedwire credit evidence tying the export proceeds to the specific shipment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT conducts targeted compliance audits of export zero-rating claims, particularly in air-cargo brokerage where paper-only export files are suspected. If the export exemption is applied without lawful justification (e.g., missing DUA, false MAWB, goods never leaving the EU, or proceeds not repatriated within 180 days), AEAT will assess output VAT at the 21% rate, add late-payment interest (interés de demora), and impose proportional penalties under Ley 58/2003: for an improper or fraudulent exemption claim, sanctions range from 50% to 150% of the tax evaded, plus a separate penalty for incorrect or false invoicing records (up to EUR 10,000 per invoice or 50% of the amount). Under the SII régime, missing electronic records trigger automatic monthly penalties of EUR 200 per anomaly. Fraudulent export zero-rating arrangements, including sham circular export schemes, are prosecuted as criminal tax fraud under arts. 305 and 305 bis of the Código Penal where the defrauded revenue exceeds EUR 120,000, carrying imprisonment of 1–6 years and fines up to six times the evaded amount; the assessment limitation period is 4 years (extending to 10 for hidden fraud), and clawback includes the full VAT plus interest and surcharges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, within the Eurosystem and subject to applicable European Central Bank regulations. Foreign-exchange and capital-movement rules are principally derived from European Union law, including the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, payment-services legislation, anti-money-laundering legislation, and applicable Spanish implementing laws. The Spanish Treasury and the Directorate-General for International Trade and Investments administer certain foreign-investment reporting and sanctions-related matters. SEPBLAC is the Spanish Financial Intelligence Unit and AML supervisory authority for relevant obliged entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and has full current-account and capital-account convertibility within the legal framework of the European Union. There is no general exchange-control approval requirement for receiving or remitting dividends, service fees, loan proceeds, trade proceeds, or liquidation distributions. A Spanish SL may generally convert euros into foreign currencies and transfer funds abroad through a regulated payment-service provider or credit institution. Principal hurdles are documentary rather than substantive: banks must establish the source and purpose of funds, identify the beneficial owner, verify tax and corporate status, screen counterparties and jurisdictions, and assess sanctions, anti-money-laundering, transfer-pricing, withholding-tax, and substance risks. Dividends require distributable accounting profits, corporate approvals, solvency compliance, and appropriate withholding-tax treatment. Payments to related non-residents must be supported by genuine agreements, arm's-length pricing, beneficial-ownership analysis, and applicable tax documentation. Payments involving sanctioned parties, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual aviation intermediaries, or opaque charter chains may be delayed or rejected.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a Spanish bank, convert a prescribed percentage of export receipts into euros, or repatriate receipts within a fixed period. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be received through foreign or European payment accounts, subject to banking, accounting, tax, customs, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering requirements. The company must retain commercial evidence supporting the transaction, including contracts, invoices, transport or charter documentation, customs evidence where applicable, counterparty information, and payment records. Cross-border transaction and external-asset reporting may apply under Banco de España statistical reporting rules, including reporting through the ETE framework where the applicable thresholds and reporting status are met. Foreign direct investment and investment-in-Spain reporting can also apply under Spanish foreign-investment regulations. There is no general mandatory conversion ratio or universal statutory conversion deadline; any bank-specific conversion covenant, account restriction, or reporting deadline must be reviewed separately.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplementary payment operations and low to medium as the sole treasury bank. A regulated European Economic Area payment institution or electronic-money institution may provide SEPA payments, virtual or operational accounts, foreign-exchange services, safeguarding, and certain international transfers through licensed partners. It is not equivalent to a credit institution: safeguarded funds are not ordinary bank deposits, credit facilities may be limited, account continuity depends on the EMI and its banking partners, and SWIFT capability, Fedwire access, cash management, documentary trade finance, and aviation-sector risk acceptance may be restricted. An offshore digital EMI without EU passporting, a Spanish or EEA licensed entity, or an appropriately regulated correspondent arrangement should not be used as the primary account for Spanish share capital, tax payments, payroll, charter settlements, or regulated client-money flows. The company must verify the provider's license, passporting status, safeguarding model, permitted services, sanctions controls, legal ownership of the account, and ability to provide Spanish or EEA payment identifiers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank can apply legally compliant electronic identification and customer-due-diligence procedures. In practice, banks may require a video interview, qualified electronic signatures, notarized or apostilled documents, certified translations, original-document review, a branch meeting, or attendance by an authorized signatory. The bank may require identification of directors, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and persons exercising control. A non-resident shareholder or director does not automatically prevent account opening, but it normally increases documentation, source-of-wealth, tax-residency, and substance requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Air-cargo charter brokerage is assessed as a medium or enhanced-risk activity because transactions may involve aircraft operators, brokers, freight forwarders, sanctioned destinations, dual-use cargo, aircraft registries, complex commissions, and high-value cross-border payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed business plan; activity description limited to brokerage or forwarding services actually performed; customer and supplier onboarding policy; sanctions and export-control policy; beneficial-owner register; sample charter, brokerage, freight-forwarding, and commission agreements; invoice flow chart; expected countries, currencies, transaction sizes, and volumes; aircraft-operator and broker licensing evidence; cargo-screening procedures; and an explanation of why the company does not handle prohibited, controlled, or sanctioned cargo.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, nominee shareholders, complex holding chains, trusts, bearer-like arrangements, or inability to identify the natural persons who ultimately own or control the SL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a current Spanish commercial-register extract; articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; tax-residency certificates; corporate resolutions; powers of attorney; and independent evidence explaining any intermediate holding company, fund, trust, or nominee relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, directors resident outside Spain, newly incorporated entity, limited Spanish operating history, or mismatch between the registered address and actual operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide lease or serviced-office evidence; director and employee information; Spanish tax registration; expected payroll and supplier profile; contracts with customers and aircraft operators; website and commercial materials; management and decision-making evidence; local professional-adviser details; and a written explanation of the operational role of Spain and the expected activity start date.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound shareholder funding or intercompany loans with unclear economic purpose, unexplained third-party remitters, round-number transfers, or funds originating from a jurisdiction unrelated to the shareholder or business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the capital-increase or loan agreement; shareholder or board resolutions; bank statements showing the source of funds; audited or management accounts of the remitter; proof of tax-paid or legitimate business income where relevant; ownership relationship documents; payment instructions showing the remitter is the investor or documented lender; and a transaction-purpose memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from high-risk, sanctioned, embargoed, or conflict-affected jurisdictions; aircraft routes, cargo origins, or counterparties associated with export-control concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide counterparty screening reports; vessel or aircraft and operator identification; route and cargo documentation; end-user and end-use statements; export or import licenses where required; sanctions-screening methodology; contractual sanctions clauses; escalation records; and evidence that no restricted party, restricted destination, or prohibited commodity is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value payments that do not reconcile with invoices, charter legs, freight documents, brokerage commissions, or the company's forecast turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a transaction-level reconciliation showing contract, invoice, service date, aircraft or route, customer, supplier, commission calculation, tax treatment, payment account, and supporting transport or delivery evidence. Maintain a rolling cash-flow forecast and notify the bank before material deviations from the onboarding profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, unrelated third-party payment accounts, cash settlements, payment splitting, rapid pass-through activity, or commingling of company funds with client or supplier funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adopt a treasury policy requiring payments from accounts held in the company's legal name; document any legally necessary third-party payment with a tripartite agreement; maintain separate operating, tax, payroll, and client-money accounts where applicable; prohibit cash except for documented minor expenses; and retain board-approved payment controls and reconciliations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent tax-residency information, missing Spanish tax identification number, unverified foreign tax forms, or unexplained withholding-tax and beneficial-ownership issues on outbound payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Spanish NIF, tax registration evidence, tax-residency certificates, group tax chart, withholding-tax analysis, treaty-relief forms where relevant, beneficial-owner declarations, transfer-pricing documentation, and confirmation that the company will comply with Spanish accounting, tax, and information-reporting obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requested Fedwire capability or U.S.-dollar clearing without a transparent U.S. commercial purpose, creating correspondent-bank sanctions and AML concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide expected USD corridors, U.S. customer or supplier contracts, invoice samples, beneficiary-bank details, reason for USD settlement, sanctions and OFAC-screening procedures, transaction-volume forecast, and evidence that every transfer will identify the originator, beneficiary, purpose, and underlying commercial document.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route share capital through a regulated Spanish or EEA credit institution or payment institution to an account in the company's legal name. The payment reference should identify the investor, capital contribution or capital increase, and the relevant corporate resolution; the bank's purpose-code or payment-message requirements should be followed because Spain does not use one universal statutory purpose-code list for every inbound corporate transfer. For a share-capital subscription, obtain bank evidence of funds receipt where required for the notarial incorporation or capital-increase process, then complete the corporate-registration steps. For shareholder loans or intercompany funding, use a signed loan agreement specifying principal, currency, maturity, interest, repayment, subordination, and use of proceeds. Reconcile the remitter name to the shareholder or documented lender and do not accept unexplained third-party funding. Retain the SWIFT or SEPA payment confirmation, bank statements, corporate resolutions, agreements, beneficial-owner evidence, and source-of-funds records. Review applicable foreign-investment declarations, Banco de España external-transaction reporting, transfer-pricing, interest-withholding, thin-capitalization or earnings-stripping, and accounting requirements before execution. For material USD transfers, use a bank capable of compliant correspondent clearing and provide complete originator, beneficiary, purpose, and underlying-contract information.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area; use SWIFT cross-border payment messaging, commonly an MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or non-euro payments. The payment file should include complete originator and beneficiary details, IBAN or account number, BIC where required, invoice number, contract reference, currency, purpose, and charge allocation. Use documentary commercial letters of credit for higher-risk or document-sensitive charter and freight transactions where the bank accepts the goods, route, transport documents, insurance, inspection, and sanctions conditions. A commercial LC should specify applicant, issuing bank, confirming or nominated bank, beneficiary, amount, expiry, shipment or service conditions, required documents, discrepancies procedure, governing rules such as UCP 600 where chosen, and sanctions and export-control compliance. For ordinary brokerage commissions, pay only against a valid agreement and invoice to the contracting counterparty's account. Apply maker-checker approval, segregation of duties, dual authorization, beneficiary verification, sanctions screening, invoice-to-contract matching, and post-payment reconciliation. Fedwire may be used for eligible USD settlements through a participating U.S. or correspondent bank, subject to the bank's cut-off times, fees, sanctions screening, and information requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a regulated bank or investment firm, documented against forecast or committed receivables and payables. The company should maintain hedge limits, tenor limits, counterparty limits, valuation records, and evidence of the underlying exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency, bank, jurisdiction, and transaction are legally and operationally eligible. Settlement is normally in a reference currency and does not deliver the restricted currency. The bank may require appropriateness, professional-client or counterparty classification, collateral, and documented underlying exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for managing recurring currency and funding exposures, subject to counterparty documentation, including an ISDA Master Agreement or equivalent, collateral terms, valuation, close-out, and EMIR requirements where applicable.

FX options, collars, and other structured hedges may be available from regulated counterparties but require enhanced suitability, risk, valuation, accounting, and board-approval controls. Avoid speculative or leveraged products outside the treasury policy.

All derivatives should be entered into with an authorized EU or appropriately regulated third-country counterparty, with MiFID II client classification and conduct requirements, EMIR reporting, risk-mitigation, clearing or margin rules where applicable, and any relevant collateral and accounting treatment reviewed. A Spanish SL should document the commercial hedge purpose, exposure amount, maturity, hedge ratio, counterparty, pricing, break costs, and authorization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual informative return of transactions with third parties (Modelo 347) when total annual transactions with a supplier or client exceed EUR 3,005.06
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the preceding calendar year: 1 February through 20 February, extended to the next business day if the 20th is a non-working day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or submission outside the mandatory window triggers fixed penalties under the Spanish General Tax Law; each omitted or inaccurate third-party transaction is fined, with a minimum penalty typically starting at EUR 1,500; registration closure is not applicable because this is a tax information filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalisation of accounting and corporate books for the preceding financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil of the company's registered office (electronic legalisation procedure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months following the financial year-end; for calendar-year entities, no later than 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalised books lose evidentiary value in court; the registry may refuse certificates and the company cannot rely on the books in litigation; continued non-compliance may contribute to inactivity grounds but does not itself produce an automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the expiration of the 6-month post-year-end filing period; for a calendar-year SL, the period is 1-25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 5% if filed within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months; late-payment interest accrues; penalties may reach up to 150% of the omitted tax due, and AEAT may seize bank accounts or credit balances; no administrative strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (deposito de cuentas anuales) after shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil of the corporate domicile and the Registro Mercantil Central for registration and openness records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the annual accounts within 6 months of the financial year-end, and the approved accounts must be deposited within 1 month after approval; for calendar-year SLs the absolute window is 1-31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit within the legal window causes 'cierre registral', meaning no other corporate instruments can be registered (e.g., director changes, share transfers) until the accounts are deposited; an administrative fine of EUR 1,200-EUR 60,000 may also be imposed; Spain does not maintain a UK-style strike-off, but a prolonged inactive company may be judicially dissolved and removed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Spanish SL must undergo a mandatory independent audit if, for two consecutive financial years, it meets at least two of the following three thresholds: total assets exceed EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; or average headcount exceeds 50 employees. An SL is also compulsorily audited if it is a public-interest entity, belongs to a group subject to consolidation, or is otherwise covered by the Spanish Auditing of Accounts Act. Air cargo charter brokers above these thresholds may not use the small-entity exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-listed Spanish limited companies must apply the Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General Contable 2007); listed entities are required to apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU. Annual accounts comprise the balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in equity, cash-flow statement, and notes, prepared under the going-concern and true-and-fair principles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not impose an annual standalone UBO confirmation statement comparable to a UK confirmation statement. Under Law 10/2010, the SL must keep current beneficial-ownership data, and any change in the register of members resulting from a share transfer must be formalised by notarial public deed and recorded in the 'Libro Registro de Socios'. The updated UBO information must be reflected in the annual accounts deposition and maintained continuously; there is no separate filing to the Mercantile Registry solely for UBO confirmation purposes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Directores), where the corporate governance structure so requires
Minute Book (Libro de Actas) for shareholder and directors' meetings
Accounting Books (Libro Diario and Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,600 per year for a registered office or corporate agent in Spain, depending on city and service scope.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 for a non-listed Spanish SL with turnover below the compulsory-audit threshold, and USD 15,000 - USD 30,000 where the air cargo charter brokerage operations meet or exceed the mandatory audit thresholds.
